title: Suppression Sticks, Locality Is Fragile: A Closed-Loop Target-and-Control Audit of Task-Vector Negation in VLA Policies
models: MergeVLA-LIBERO (Qwen2.5-0.5B + dinosiglip + 0.16B action expert, continuous regression head)
action_head: mixed: regression head (MergeVLA), discrete action tokens (OpenVLA), flow/diffusion action expert (pi0.5)
methods: task-vector negation theta_goal - alpha * tau_i (weight-space edit, not activation steering)
closed-loop target-and-control matrices (every skill evaluated after each edit)
NegGrad, NegGrad+, Gradient-Difference and leave-one-out retraining baselines
question: When a per-skill task vector is subtracted from a multitask VLA, is the target skill removed and are the other skills left intact in closed-loop execution?
key_findings: Full LIBERO-Goal 10x10 matrix (MergeVLA, alpha = 1, 20 rollouts/cell): 5 skills separate (target <= 15%, controls >= 40%, baseline-normalized retention 57.8%), 3 resist suppression, 2 collapse every control.

Held-out initial states at selected alpha*: all 5 suppressible targets stay at 0/20, but mean normalized control retention is 52% (range 78% to 4%) and 4 of 5 edits drive at least one unrelated control to 0%.
Direction-specific: a norm-matched random direction removes only about 25% of the target; equal-norm re-addition leaves the target at 50%.
Locus: VLM-only negation matches full negation, action-head-only leaves the target at 80%; restricting the edit to any single depth band leaves the target largely intact (mean 91% retained).
Cross-suite: no clean separation on LIBERO-Spatial; Object and Long10 suppress targets but keep only 5.8% and 11.7% off-diagonal control SR.

Cross-architecture: OpenVLA-7B suppresses all 3 diagnostic targets to 0% with mean off-diagonal control 50.8%; pi0.5 shows positive target-control gaps (30.0-68.3 pp) on a 4-skill Goal panel, one row non-selective.
Multi-skill negation collapses the policy: controls fall to 10% at k = 2 and everything to 0% for k >= 3, even with norm-matched scaling.

Weight-space cosine does not predict collateral damage (VLM task vectors near-orthogonal, cos about 0.011-0.014; Spearman rho = -0.03 vs collateral drop over 56 cells); action-head vectors more aligned (cos about 0.26).
Gradient baselines on a matched panel: NegGrad zeroes all controls, Gradient-Difference keeps 88.3% control SR vs 73.9% for negation, retraining oracle 95.6%.

Relearning: the negated model recovers t0 to 85% (17/20) after 250 steps while a task-naive base is still 0/20; CKA between intact and negated hidden states stays 0.84-0.93, consistent with behavioral masking, not unlearning.

evidence.scale: 20 rollouts per cell (OpenVLA off-diagonals 10, some pi0.5 cells 10); selection on initial states 0-19, held-out validation on 20-39; one training seed for full matrices, 3-seed probe for t0
evidence.statistics: yes: raw counts with 95% Wilson intervals, paired designs, row-bootstrap CI (53.3 pp gap, CI [45.7, 61.0]), Fisher test for pi0.5 dose-response; explicit caveats that post-hoc subgroup tests are descriptive
evidence.baselines: no-edit model, norm-matched random direction, NegGrad (500-2000 steps), NegGrad+, Gradient-Difference, leave-one-task-out retraining oracle

causal_validation: Yes, every claim is from closed-loop rollouts after a weight intervention, with random-direction, sign, anchor, component and depth controls. The paper explicitly says its geometric and loss-landscape diagnostics characterize but do not explain the effect.
closed_loop: Yes, all target and control success rates are closed-loop LIBERO rollouts.
limitations_stated: Single training seed for the full matrices; a three-seed probe only for one target.
Simulation only (LIBERO MuJoCo); no real robot.
Clean selectivity requires per-skill expert task vectors; negating an off-the-shelf multitask vector is broadly destructive.
Selectivity fails on Object and Long-horizon suites.
Gradient-baseline comparison covers one target, one seed, one budget per method.
critique: Methodologically the most careful paper in this batch: held-out initial states for the selected operating point, Wilson intervals, matched controls, and explicit separation of descriptive vs confirmatory claims.

It is weight-space editing, not activation steering; it belongs in the steering section as the main evidence that 'suppression works' does not imply 'edit is local', a lesson that applies to activation steering too (most steering papers report only the target behavior).
20 rollouts per cell gives wide intervals (0/20 -> [0, 16]%), so per-cell control damage claims are noisy; the regime taxonomy depends on fixed thresholds (shown stable across 30-40%).
The relearning result and high CKA support the view that edits mask behavior rather than remove knowledge, which matters for safety-oriented unlearning claims elsewhere.
one_line: Subtracting a per-skill task vector from a multitask VLA reliably switches the target skill off in closed loop, but often breaks unrelated skills, fails on suites with shared motions, and is easily re-learned, so it masks rather than removes.
